A national broadcaster's report (26 March 2026): the country's parliament passed a bill amending the 2019 transgender-rights act that removes the right to self-identify, limits recognition to biological/physical traits (including intersex variations and traditional community identities) certified by medical boards and district authorities, and mandates certification for gender-affirming surgery; protests followed, the estimated ~2 million transgender population faces uneven recognition, and a supreme-court-appointed panel asked the government to withdraw the bill as contrary to the 2014 self-identification ruling.

A national newspaper's city report (18 August 2024): a trans woman alleged a railway-security constable groped her as a 'gender check' at a metro station and made a lewd remark; the railway police denied it and filed a counter-complaint — recorded as an instance of security-force practice treating trans presentation as itself grounds for invasive 'gender verification' at transport checkpoints, in a case that reached the courts on the complainants' side.
